item.case_name: Fact piece about a real thing
item.title: Meet the Real F-35A

turns.text: Make an 8-second widescreen mini-documentary introducing the real F-35A Lightning II. Show it taking off from a runway, then flying. Label it 'F-35A Lightning II', with 'One engine' and 'Conventional takeoff' appearing in turn. Calm English narration explaining those two facts. Real aircraft proportions, not a sci-fi jet.

item.tests: Tests whether a short factual aircraft film preserves the named variant's visible geometry and operating characteristics.

answer_sheet.Aircraft and variant: The real F-35A Lightning II, not the F-35B or F-35C.
answer_sheet.On-screen wording: F-35A Lightning II; One engine; Conventional takeoff.
answer_sheet.Narration: Calm English narration explaining that the F-35A has one engine and takes off conventionally from a runway; exact wording and voice are your call.
answer_sheet.Visual style and setting: Realistic documentary imagery; runway location, weather and camera angles are your call.
answer_sheet.Music: Your call, provided the narration remains clear.

must_haves: The aircraft has the recognizable F-35 configuration: one rear engine exhaust, two outward-canted vertical tails and no canards.
The takeoff shows a forward runway roll and lift-off, not hovering or a vertical launch.
The same aircraft design remains consistent between the runway and airborne views.
All three requested labels appear exactly and are legible.
Audible English narration correctly describes one engine and conventional runway takeoff without attributing F-35B hover capability to the F-35A.

stages.text:
F-35A Lightning II — First Flight
kind: documentary
style: Live-action widescreen documentary realism; steady tracking views, natural daylight, and AA-1’s documented proportions, geometry and markings.
In the opening two seconds, a widescreen live-action view shows AA-1, the first F-35A Lightning II prototype, lifting off at Lockheed Martin in Fort Worth, Texas, at 12:44 p.m. Central Standard Time on December 15, 2006. The title reads “F-35A Lightning II.” Chief pilot Jon Beesley remains an indistinct silhouette beneath the dark canopy.

The gray aircraft rises nose-high above the pale runway, with its nose gear and both main landing-gear assemblies extended. Its pointed nose, slender test probe, swept wings, side intakes and two outward-canted tail fins match the documented aircraft. From seconds two through five, “One engine” appears; calm English narration says, “The F-35A has one engine.”

From seconds five through eight, the view follows AA-1 flying after departure. “Conventional takeoff” replaces the previous fact label, while the narrator says, “It takes off from a conventional runway.” These successive views show an excerpt of the inaugural development test flight, not its full thirty-five-minute duration.
stages.note: research: The F-35A Lightning II’s first flight: prototype AA-1 taking off at Fort Worth, Texas, on December 15, 2006. For the eight-second film, show runway acceleration and liftoff, then an airborne view. Keep 'F-35A Lightning II' visible; introduce 'One engine' and 'Conventional takeoff' in turn. Suggested calm English narration: 'The F-35A Lightning II. One engine. Conventional takeoff from a runway.'

items.prompt: Live-action widescreen documentary realism, steady tracking views, natural daylight, and historically accurate AA-1 geometry and markings. 0–2 s: A continuous 16:9 telephoto tracking shot shows gray F-35A prototype AA-1 lifting off rightward at Lockheed Martin in Fort Worth, Texas, at 12:44 p.m. CST on December 15, 2006. Pale runway, dry yellow-brown grass, leafless trees and distant vehicles sit beneath pale blue sky. Match the reference photograph: pointed nose with slender test probe, dark canopy, side intakes, swept wings, two outward-canted tail fins, one rear exhaust, small forward-fuselage flags and historical markings. Keep authentic F-35A proportions, not a sci-fi jet. Chief pilot Jon Beesley is only an indistinct silhouette. Nose raised, nose gear and both main gear assemblies extended, light struts and dark tires. White sans-serif title “F-35A Lightning II” appears upper left. 2–5 s: Track smoothly as AA-1 rises; the runway drops lower. Clear the title and show “One engine” lower left. A calm adult English narrator with a measured documentary delivery says exactly: “The F-35A has one engine.” 5–8 s: Continue tracking the same AA-1 flying in a shallow climb, gear still extended. Replace the fact label with “Conventional takeoff” lower left. The same narrator says exactly: “It takes off from a conventional runway.” Finish speech before the end. Natural single-engine jet roar stays beneath the voice. This is an excerpt of the inaugural development flight, not the entire sortie. No other text, no cuts, no music, no subtitles.
